full_caption: Wendell Alderidge, Appellant, v. Cordelia Lowbridge, Appellee
court: Northridge Land and Property Court, Harrowgate Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Wendell Alderidge, the association governing the Saltmarsh subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Cordelia Lowbridge from maintaining a detached structure at 4443 Ferndale Road, Harrowgate, NR in violation of Article V of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article VIII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Article V prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Cordelia Lowbridge measures 1,180 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Covenants are construed in favor of the free use of land. Ambiguity in a restriction is resolved against the party seeking to enforce it, and a restriction will not be extended by implication to conduct not fairly within its terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The defense of changed conditions requires a showing that the character of the neighborhood has so altered that the original purpose of the restriction can no longer be achieved. Isolated violations elsewhere in the subdivision do not meet that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 18 comparable violations over a period of 15 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The business judgment rule shields the board's maintenance and budgeting decisions from judicial second-guessing where the board acted within its authority, on an informed basis, and in the honest belief that the action served the association.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The association's architectural review committee denied the application by letter dated February 3, 2031. The declaration requires that denials state the specific ground relied upon; the letter recited only that the proposal was 'not in harmony with the community.'

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ASSESSMENTS, LIENS AND PRIORITY
sections.text: Annual assessments are levied against each Lot in equal shares and are due on the first day of each fiscal year. Unpaid assessments bear interest at 9 percent per annum and become a lien upon recording of a notice of assessment lien in the Harrowgate County land records. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage of record predating the notice and superior to all other subsequently recorded encumbrances. The Association shall furnish an estoppel statement of amounts due within 15 days of written request.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — LEASING RESTRICTION
sections.text: No Lot may be leased for a term of less than 24 months, and no more than 5 percent of the Lots may be leased at any one time. An owner in possession on the date this Rider was recorded is exempt as to that Lot until title is transferred. This Rider does not apply to a lease to a family member of the owner or to occupancy incident to a mortgagee's possession following foreclosure.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.
